author: @Gamerfigirl
text:
I came across an interesting use case for agent commerce while exploring a new campaign on TermiX.

The Four Meme × MonoPoly Market campaign has 3,800 slots, with 760 USDT already committed to escrow.

The task itself is pretty simple:

🔸 Follow three specified X accounts.
🔸 Submit proof of each follow.
🔸 Get 0.20 USDT and 50 TermiX Points after approval.

One of the requirements even asks for a screen recording instead of just a screenshot.

At first glance, this looks like another small social bounty, but the mechanics behind it are worth examining.

The 760 USDT is deposited into escrow before participants start completing tasks. Each approved submission releases 0.20 USDT from that pool.

The brand has up to three days to review submissions, and providers can challenge rejected work through the platform’s arbitration process.

That creates an interesting economic problem.

When you’re dealing with a few large transactions, manually reviewing deliverables might be manageable.

But what happens when a marketplace starts processing thousands of microjobs, each with its own submission, verification requirements and potential disputes?

The cost of reviewing work, handling disagreements and maintaining accountability can quickly become more important than the actual reward.

This is where I think TermiX’s approach becomes interesting.

Its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol is designed around more than matching buyers with service providers.

It brings together:

🔸 On-chain escrow for funded jobs.
🔸 Defined acceptance criteria for deliverables.
🔸 Challenge mechanisms for disputed submissions.
🔸 Independent evaluators for arbitration.
🔸 Reputation built around settled outcomes.

The bigger opportunity is making small digital tasks economically viable without relying entirely on a central marketplace operator to manage trust.

I think microjobs are an interesting testing ground for this infrastructure because they expose the less glamorous problems of agent commerce.

Paying someone is easy.

Making sure the work is completed, verified and fairly settled at scale is where things get interesting.

I’ll be watching how these campaign submissions actually move through settlement.

Over time, the Indian economy has steadily moved away from its dependence on agriculture. The majority of the value added to the Indian economy now comes from the services sector, while industry contributes about a quarter of the economic value added.

To varying extents, most Indian states too reflect this trend, but the contribution of industry differs across Indian states. Industry accounted for over 40% of the economy in only a few states like Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand in 2022. In Sikkim, industry’s share was over 60% for the same year.

Gujarat is an outlier among richer states, with manufacturing contributing more to its economy than services. In other richer states, such as Kerala and Karnataka, services account for more than 60% of the state's GDP.

Industry includes manufacturing, construction, mining and utilities such as electricity and water supply.

🎯🎯🎯PI NETWORK NEWS: Pi Ecosystem Summit Begins Today!

Pi Ecosystem Summit Day 1: Developer Platform, Ecosystem Initiatives & Showcases

PCT source : https://t.co/tJE6D0NyC8

Pi Network’s first-ever Ecosystem Summit begins today! Over the next three days, the online Summit will feature new developer platform announcements, conversations with developers, and technical demos, highlighting the tools and applications helping expand Pi’s utility across the ecosystem.

Here is the schedule for today’s video program:

- Opening remarks with Pi Network Founder, Chengdiao Fan.
- Pi AI/MCP Demo: Demo of the Developer Web Console and MCP tools for AI-assisted app development, with Pi Network Founder Nicolas Kokkalis.
- Pi Subscription Smart Contract Demo: Demo of on-chain subscription smart contract functionality for recurring payments.
- OpenMind x402 Demo: Demonstration of x402-compatible Pi payments through RoboPay on Pi Testnet.
- CiDi Games Discussion: Pi Founder Chengdiao Fan and a CiDi Games Co-founder, Jeremy Ng, talk about building on Pi, gaming utility, and developer experiences.

Watch today’s Summit video premiere below at 8:00 AM PST / 4:00 PM UTC! 
https://t.co/GxaFVfkUsD
The Summit continues tomorrow, November 18 with additional technical demos and developer conversations, and new announcements!

November 19 kicks off an all-new Pi hackathon, Pi Next, with a 200,000 USDT prize pool, offering developers the opportunity to build real-world applications for Pi’s large, KYC-verified user base using Pi’s developer platform, SDKs, and built-in Pi Authentication and payment capabilities.

Visit the Pi Ecosystem Summit landing page for all Summit content, including video presentations (https://t.co/U2ulM8DwGG), announcements, technical demos, and hackathon information. The page will be updated throughout the three-day event as new content is released.

Read on for more details of the new tools, features, programs and key announcements from Day 1 of the Ecosystem Summit!

Building and Growing Applications on Pi

In the era of increasingly accessible AI development, reaching users and sustaining engagement are important challenges for developers. Pi addresses both sides of this process by providing tools that simplify application development, and an existing ecosystem where developers can connect their products with real users.

Pi offers builders access to a global community of 60 million+ Engaged Pioneers, an ecosystem of decentralized human infrastructure (https://t.co/b4GxXUTMSE), and a network of 420,000+ Nodes. Pi’s infrastructure also provides developers with user authentication, Pi payments, verified identity, AI-compatible development, monetization and application discovery capabilities, helping them bring their applications to an established community of Pioneers and turn Pi’s platform and collective resources into practical utility.

AI-Assisted Development: New Developer Web Console and MCP

Developers and creators can now use AI agents to build and register applications, integrate them with Pi’s APIs, and apply for app listing in the Pi ecosystem! This new AI-assisted developer experience streamlines the process of bringing applications to Pi and reduces much of the friction and effort in traditional developer onboarding and integration.

Through a new browser-based Developer Web Console with Pi’s developer tools built on Model Context Protocol (MCP) (https://t.co/siNDJiZyR7); https://t.co/9xwZAF45uu), developers can connect compatible AI coding agents to Pi’s developer tools and use natural-language instructions to perform supported setup and integration tasks. This includes creating and registering Pi applications, configuring application settings and URLs, and implementing Pi APIs such as Pi Authentication and Pi Payments (https://t.co/seJdd19h6B.

Rather than manually navigating multiple configuration steps, documentation pages, and developer interfaces, developers can use AI agents to handle much of the technical setup and implementation, with human authorization where required. The Developer Web Console also provides a centralized interface for managing applications and accessing developer resources, supporting both traditional development and AI-assisted workflows. These capabilities are intended for developers building new applications as well as those bringing existing applications to Pi, including professional developers, startups, and creators using AI coding tools.

More broadly, this reduces the technical barriers to building on Pi, making the platform more accessible to a wider range of creators while simplifying the development and integration process. Today, Pi Network Founder Dr. Nicolas Kokkalis hosts a demo on how an AI agent can interact with Pi’s developer tools to take an application through the process of registration, configuration, and integration with Pi’s platform.

New Ecosystem Growth Incentives and Marketing Budget

Pi Network is announcing App Growth Initiative: a new initiative with a marketing budget of up to 20 million Pi. Sponsored by the Pi Foundation, this initiative can help developers attract users and encourage greater participation in Pi ecosystem applications.

Under the initiative, eligible developers can qualify for access to a portion of this marketing budget based on the merits and performance of their applications. Developers can then leverage the Pi-funded incentive program to reach and engage KYC-verified users without having to fund the rewards themselves. For example, when an eligible KYC-verified Pioneer invites another eligible KYC-verified Pioneer to use a participating app, both the referring Pioneer and the new user could each receive some Pi from the Foundation-sponsored incentive budget for qualifying participation. More details on exact eligibility requirements and reward amounts will be announced later.

The program is designed to help developers reach Pi’s existing network of identity-verified, Mainnet-migrated users without needing to independently fund and build their own referral and user-acquisition programs. The overall incentive budget may be allocated among participating applications based on factors such as app quality, utility, and demonstrated user engagement, with stronger-performing apps potentially qualifying for greater support.

More broadly, the App Growth Initiative aims to extend Pi’s network-growth infrastructure to ecosystem developers. It embeds the funding into user growth mechanisms, which apply some of the strategies Pi has developed through growing its own network. The initiative channels those resources through proven growth mechanisms designed to help apps acquire and engage real users. This approach improves support for developers while helping ensure that the network’s ecosystem-growth resources are deployed efficiently and tied to actual user participation.

Developer Incentives and Redesigned Pi App Directory

Pi is introducing new mechanisms to incentivize developers to build high-quality, engaging applications. Developer incentive programs often reward developers through visibility, financial incentives, or status. Visibility provides better distribution opportunities; financial incentives may include development cost subsidies or discounts (e.g. Pi App Studio’s subsidized pricing rate for creators whose apps demonstrate real utility and attract real users) (https://t.co/s7jdig1rfV), and status rewards provide indicators of developer reputation.

As part of implementing these developer incentive mechanisms, Pi has launched a major redesign of the Pi App Directory, introducing new ways for Pioneers to discover applications and expanding visibility opportunities for developers to reach users across the ecosystem.

While the directory maintains Ecosystem Directory Staking as a core discovery and ranking mechanism (https://t.co/7oI9Fkg8OM), additional discovery sections that highlight applications based on user interest, growth, and engagement have been introduced:

- Bookmarked Apps: Makes it easier for Pioneers to access and return to their favorite apps.
- Pi-Staked Apps: Maintains the existing community staking-based app ranking mechanism.
- Rising Apps: Highlights newer apps gaining traction.
- Discover: Introduces Pioneers to applications they haven’t tried.
- Pioneers Keep Coming Back: Features apps identified for repeat user engagement. 
These updates provide channels for new apps to get exposure based on merits. Developers are incentivized to build better and engaging apps to get rewarded with more visibility. 

Together, these changes represent a broader effort to strengthen application distribution within Pi. By creating more opportunities for apps to gain visibility through genuine user engagement, the redesigned app directory encourages developers to prioritize useful, high-quality products while helping Pioneers discover more ways to use Pi.

Pi Launchpad, DEX, and AMM Coming to Mainnet in Q1 2027

Pi Launchpad, decentralized exchange (DEX), and automated market maker (AMM) capabilities will be launching on Mainnet in Q1 2027! These capabilities have been on Testnet and went through multiple cycles of iterations, and they will provide additional infrastructure for ecosystem token launches, supporting developers and applications that incorporate tokens for specific utility purposes.

This commitment establishes a timeframe for developers and ecosystem participants to prepare for Mainnet token launches. As Pi continues introducing new tools, resources and programs that simplify application development and engage a wider range of developers, Pi Launchpad, DEX, and AMM will provide additional infrastructure to support the next stage of ecosystem development.

The Q1 2027 timeline also allows potential Launchpad candidates, including projects participating in Pi’s upcoming hackathon, time to build and prepare applications for possible token launches.

On-Chain Subscription Smart Contracts

Pi’s on-chain subscription smart contract enables developers to build recurring payment services into their applications (https://t.co/RBW3UB04Ih), supporting use cases such as service memberships, gaming, online tools, streaming platforms, and other subscription-based products.

First introduced on Pi Testnet in April 2026 (https://t.co/n42tNqvC4V), the capability addresses a common challenge with blockchain-based subscriptions. While subscriptions are widely used in traditional digital services, implementing them on blockchains has often required repeated transaction authorization, upfront funding, or additional infrastructure.

Pi’s implementation allows users to authorize a defined spending budget and subscription period, such as 6 months for a monthly subscription, without signing every renewal. Users can extend or cancel their subscriptions, and funds remain in their own wallets until each payment is processed rather than being locked or transferred upfront.

Now, in addition to the smart contract itself, any associated supporting infrastructure such as in Pi Wallet and the developer platform have been implemented to support the full experience of subscriptions for users and developers. 

The Day 1 Pi Network demo showcases how developers can integrate this Testnet functionality into their applications, including subscription configuration, user authorization, and payment processing.

x402 Payments Integrated on Pi Testnet

x402 is an open payment protocol that uses the HTTP 402 Payment Required response to allow services to request payment as part of a web interaction, without requiring traditional checkout processes. As AI agents become increasingly capable of performing tasks independently, x402 enables new ways for software and machines to transact with one another more efficiently, including paying for accessing digital services or completing automated tasks.

Pi Network has implemented support for x402 payments on Pi Testnet, enabling applications, APIs, AI agents, and automated services to make programmatic Test-Pi payments. Pi’s submitted specification covers both Pi Testnet and Pi Mainnet, and more details on Mainnet availability will be shared ahead of its launch. 

Today, OpenMind demonstrates an integration of Pi payments with its RoboPay platform using the x402 payment standard on Pi Testnet. The demo shows how developers can configure Pi as an accepted form of payment and how an automated client can request a robot or service action, pay in Test-Pi, and trigger the requested action once the payment is completed.

Pi has submitted its technical specification for x402 payments to the x402 Foundation, where it is in the review process for inclusion in the official x402 specification. The integration is already functional, as today’s demo shows.

Additional Developer Platform Features

Beyond the features demonstrated at today’s Summit, Pi has introduced several additional features to support developers building applications in the ecosystem.

Improved End-User Onboarding and Deep Linking for Pi Apps
Pi has improved the onboarding experience for users accessing ecosystem applications through PiNet links. When someone receives and opens a PiNet app link without Pi Browser installed, they are prompted to download Pi Browser through the App Store or Google Play. After installing and opening the Pi Browser, they will be redirected to the original Pi application or page they intended to visit. For example, if someone outside of Pi Network is invited by a Pioneer to play a game on a Pi app, they will be able to play that game session directly after the onboarding without having to figure out navigation to the game manually. 

This smooth deep linking functionality ensures continuity of the user experience of Pi apps for users outside of the network, and reduces the dropoff rate of user conversion in their growth efforts, thus making it easier for developers to bring people directly to their applications.

Notification Center
Pi is introducing an in-app Notification Center that enables developers to send users ecosystem notifications from their Pi apps, and allows users to see the notifications in one place in the Pi ecosystem. All ecosystem developers can begin integrating this functionality now, allowing their apps to send relevant notifications to users, support interactions, and encourage continued engagement. These notifications are delivered within the Pi Browser, rather than as push notifications to users’ phones. 

Access to push notifications natively is the next step for the Notification Center, subject to more selective and restrictive rules for developers to prevent spamming and ensure well-intended uses.

During the initial rollout, applications can send notifications to up to 20 users without additional approval. Developers seeking to notify more users will need approval, a temporary measure intended to prevent spam as the new feature expands.

Building What’s Next

Day 1 of the Pi Ecosystem Summit highlights Pi’s continued efforts to improve the developer experience and strengthen the tools, infrastructure, and incentives supporting ecosystem development. Together, these initiatives help developers build useful applications, reach real users, and create more opportunities for Pioneers to participate in the ecosystem.

Developers can explore Pi’s Developer Console to get started, and visit the Pi Ecosystem Summit landing page for the full program (https://t.co/osxhyx9Ipz), additional announcements, technical demos, and upcoming hackathon information (https://t.co/U2ulM8DwGG) 🎯🎯🎯

@hbr_pbc and @GoogleDeepMind are hosting the world's first Robot Use Agent (RUA) hackathon with Gemini 4 Carbon, right here in Singapore.

The most creative hacks stand a chance to win cash prizes, and the robotics teams in the room will be scouting for cracked talent to join them full-time!

Sign-ups close November 25.

When and where: Sunday, November 29, 9am to 7pm, Lorong AI @ One-North, Singapore.

Cash Prizes (USD):
1st: $2,500 and an M6 Mac Mini
2nd: $1,250
3rd: $750

Full-time Role Opportunities: open to all participants.

Every team gets an SO-101 robot arm on the day. Feel free to bring your own if your build needs more, plus any props, tools and equipment (anything your project needs to come to life).

Teams of 4 (strictly) get one day to build the most creative robot applications they can with Hebbian's RUA SDK and Gemini 4 credits.

Judges from @GoogleDeepMind, @ycombinator, @cortexairobot, @daqstra, @bifrost_ai, @menloresearch and @therobotgrp will pick the winners!

Who it's for:

- Robotics & mechatronics engineers

- Software & ML engineers excited about AI/robotics

- Students and early-career engineers in AI/robotics

Why we're doing this:
Computer Use Agents (CUA) let AI operate software. Robot Use Agents (RUA) enable autonomous work in the physical world. You describe the task in plain language, the way you would to a coworker, and agents work out the rest.

With RUA, you give a frontier model a goal, camera views and a set of robot tools, and it controls the robot to do the task.

Once telling a robot what to do is as simple as a conversation, the cost of programming robots for autonomous work drops from months to days.

We believe this will unlock an abundance of robotics applications, especially ones that were previously cost-prohibitive, much like what coding agents have done for software.

Lunch and tea will be provided. Form your team beforehand or on the day.

Sure, if there’s a cash/tax component or any other out-of-pocket cost, that’s real money, fair enough.

But netting a points redemption against cash is like saying, “I’ve got a 100% off discount code to cover this bill… but you still owe me the cash.”
